name: Aprepitant
route_note: Oral capsules or suspension over three days with chemotherapy; IV emulsion; fosaprepitant IV prodrug
owner: Merck & Co. (Emend); Heron Therapeutics (Cinvanti, Aponvie); generic

discovery.note: A morpholine NK1 antagonist that crosses the blood–brain barrier, first explored as an antidepressant.

tagline: First NK1 antagonist, preventing delayed chemotherapy-induced vomiting
summary: Aprepitant blocks the neurokinin-1 receptor for substance P. Added to a 5-HT3 antagonist and dexamethasone, it reduces both acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, and an IV form is used for postoperative nausea.
mechanism: Substance P released in the brainstem's emetic centres acts on NK1 receptors to drive vomiting, especially in the delayed phase after chemotherapy that 5-HT3 antagonists control poorly.

Aprepitant crosses into the central nervous system and occupies NK1 receptors with high selectivity. It is a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and an inducer of CYP2C9, creating interactions with dexamethasone, warfarin and hormonal contraceptives.
uses: Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting with highly and moderately emetogenic chemotherapy
Prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting

history.title: Antidepressant study
history.detail: Merck reports antidepressant activity of an NK1 antagonist in Science; later phase 3 depression trials fail.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Emend for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

history.title: Postoperative nausea
history.detail: Oral aprepitant is approved for postoperative nausea and vomiting.

history.title: Fosaprepitant
history.detail: FDA approves the IV prodrug fosaprepitant (Emend for injection).

history.title: IV emulsion
history.detail: FDA approves Cinvanti, a polysorbate-free IV aprepitant emulsion.

history.title: Aponvie
history.detail: FDA approves Aponvie IV aprepitant for postoperative nausea and vomiting.

facts: Aprepitant began as a candidate antidepressant before being developed as an antiemetic.
Dexamethasone doses are reduced when given with aprepitant because of CYP3A4 inhibition.
